    Joint RNA and ATAC analysis with bixverse¶

    Intro¶

    10x multiome measures gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the same nuclei. This vignette takes the unsorted 3k PBMC data set (Cell Ranger ARC 2.0.0) from the raw files to linked peaks and genes: fragment QC and multiplet calls, peaks called per cluster, TF-IDF and LSI, the weighted nearest neighbour graph over both modalities, gene activity and label transfer, differential accessibility and peak to gene links.

    ATAC lives next to the RNA in a SingleCellsMultiModal: a second v5 store under atac/ with peaks as features, log-CPM as the norm until run_tfidf switches it to TF-IDF, and the genomic coordinates in an interval index. Its cells are the RNA cells, in the same order, so the RNA cell filter applies to both. Read the multi-modal vignette first if you have not. ATAC without RNA has its own vignette.

    Motif analysis (chromVAR) and coverage tracks are not in bixverse yet.

    In [1]:
    Copied!

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

import bixverse as bv
import bixverse.embed

    The data¶

    download_pbmc_multiome fetches the filtered feature barcode matrix (RNA and Cell Ranger's peak counts in one h5), the fragment file with its tabix index, Cell Ranger's peaks, the GENCODE v32 annotation Cell Ranger ARC's GRCh38 reference was built from, and the ENCODE hg38 blacklist.

gtf = data_dir / "gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz"

    Loading¶

    The RNA comes from the Gene Expression rows of the h5, the ATAC from its Peaks rows. add_atac_tenx writes the peak store for every cell of the RNA store, in its order; it counts Tn5 insertions, as Cell Ranger does.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    bv.io.load_tenx_h5(exp_dir, h5_path)
mm = bv.SingleCellsMultiModal(exp_dir)
bv.atac.add_atac_tenx(mm, h5_path)
mm

    Quality control¶

    Per cell from the fragment file: fragments, nucleosome signal (mono- over nucleosome-free fragments), TSS enrichment, the fraction on chrM and the fraction of insertions in peaks. Cell Ranger ARC leaves chrM out of the fragment file, so the ATAC mito fraction is zero throughout here; the RNA side has its own.

    The two library-level checks first: insertions pile up at TSSs, and fragment lengths come in nucleosome steps. A flat TSS profile or a smooth length distribution means a failed library, whatever the per-cell numbers say.

bv.pl.tss_profile_plot(tss_profile, ax=axes[0])
bv.pl.fragment_length_plot(frag_lengths, ax=axes[1])
plt.show()

    Multiplets¶

    Nuclei carry two copies of each chromosome, so a locus covered by more than two of a cell's fragments points at a second nucleus. AMULET counts those loci per cell and tests them against a Poisson background, without clustering or RNA. Regions that pile up fragments in every cell, the blacklist, are left out; a repeat list would clean the calls further.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    amulet = bv.atac.amulet(mm, fragments, restrict_beds=[blacklist])
print(f"{amulet['amulet_multiplet'].sum()} of {amulet.height} cells called multiplets")
    amulet = bv.atac.amulet(mm, fragments, restrict_beds=[blacklist]) print(f"{amulet['amulet_multiplet'].sum()} of {amulet.height} cells called multiplets")
    113 of 2956 cells called multiplets

    Thresholds¶

    On the ATAC side we keep cells with 1,000 to 100,000 insertions in peaks, a nucleosome signal under 2 and a TSS enrichment over 2, cut-offs that sit in the tails of the distributions above. On the RNA side we flag MAD outliers on library size and genes, and cells above 3 MADs of mitochondrial share.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    atac_metrics = {
    "atac_lib_size": obs["atac_lib_size"].to_numpy(),
    "atac_nucleosome_signal": obs["atac_nucleosome_signal"].to_numpy(),
    "atac_tss_enrichment": obs["atac_tss_enrichment"].to_numpy(),
}
atac_calls = bv.qc.run_cell_qc_fixed(
    atac_metrics,
    obs["cell_idx"].to_numpy(),
    {
        "atac_lib_size": {"lower": 1000, "upper": 100_000},
        "atac_nucleosome_signal": {"upper": 2},
        "atac_tss_enrichment": {"lower": 2},
    },
)
bv.pl.violin_plot(atac_calls)
plt.show()
    atac_metrics = { "atac_lib_size": obs["atac_lib_size"].to_numpy(), "atac_nucleosome_signal": obs["atac_nucleosome_signal"].to_numpy(), "atac_tss_enrichment": obs["atac_tss_enrichment"].to_numpy(), } atac_calls = bv.qc.run_cell_qc_fixed( atac_metrics, obs["cell_idx"].to_numpy(), { "atac_lib_size": {"lower": 1000, "upper": 100_000}, "atac_nucleosome_signal": {"upper": 2}, "atac_tss_enrichment": {"lower": 2}, }, ) bv.pl.violin_plot(atac_calls) plt.show()

    Highly variable genes, PCA, kNN, Leiden. These clusters are what the peaks get called on below.

    Peaks¶

    Cell Ranger calls peaks on all cells pooled, which under-calls rare populations. We call them per RNA cluster with bixverse's port of MACS3 callpeak (--nomodel --extsize 200 --shift -100 on the Tn5 insertions), merge the clusters' peaks, drop those on the standard chromosomes' blacklist regions and on contigs, and recount the fragments against the merged set. The new store replaces the Cell Ranger one.

    In [14]:
    Copied! 
    cr_peaks = mm.var(modality="atac").height
peaks = bv.atac.call_peaks(mm, fragments, group_by="leiden_clustering")
peaks = peaks.filter(pl.col("chrom").str.contains(r"^chr[0-9XY]+$"))
peaks = bv.atac.remove_blacklisted(peaks, blacklist)
print(f"Cell Ranger peaks: {cr_peaks}, merged per-cluster peaks: {peaks.height}")
bv.atac.add_atac_fragments(mm, fragments, peaks=peaks, overwrite=True)
bv.atac.annotate_peaks(mm, gtf)
mm.var(modality="atac").head()
    cr_peaks = mm.var(modality="atac").height peaks = bv.atac.call_peaks(mm, fragments, group_by="leiden_clustering") peaks = peaks.filter(pl.col("chrom").str.contains(r"^chr[0-9XY]+$")) peaks = bv.atac.remove_blacklisted(peaks, blacklist) print(f"Cell Ranger peaks: {cr_peaks}, merged per-cluster peaks: {peaks.height}") bv.atac.add_atac_fragments(mm, fragments, peaks=peaks, overwrite=True) bv.atac.annotate_peaks(mm, gtf) mm.var(modality="atac").head()

    TF-IDF and LSI¶

    TF-IDF over the kept cells, then a truncated SVD of the TF-IDF. We keep peaks above the 25th percentile of total counts: the bottom quarter is mostly noise at this depth. The first LSI component of ATAC data usually tracks sequencing depth rather than cell identity; calculate_lsi leaves it out of the embedding by default, and the depth plot shows whether that is right here (hollow points are the components left out).

    In [15]:
    Copied! 
    bv.atac.run_tfidf(mm)
top = bv.atac.find_top_features(mm, min_cutoff="q25")
print(f"{top.size} of {mm.var(modality='atac').height} peaks kept for the LSI")
bv.atac.calculate_lsi(mm, n_comp=50)
bv.pl.lsi_depth_plot(bv.atac.get_lsi_depth_cor(mm))
plt.show()
    bv.atac.run_tfidf(mm) top = bv.atac.find_top_features(mm, min_cutoff="q25") print(f"{top.size} of {mm.var(modality='atac').height} peaks kept for the LSI") bv.atac.calculate_lsi(mm, n_comp=50) bv.pl.lsi_depth_plot(bv.atac.get_lsi_depth_cor(mm)) plt.show()

    The RNA clusters stay together on the ATAC UMAP: the two modalities come from the same nuclei.

    Weighted nearest neighbours¶

    WNN fuses the RNA PCA and the ATAC LSI per cell, weighting each by how well it predicts the cell's neighbourhood.

    In [17]:
    Copied! 
    bv.mm.generate_wnn_graph(
    mm,
    modality_2="atac",
    embd_to_use_2="lsi",
    no_embd_to_use_1=30,
    no_embd_to_use_2=30,
)
bv.graph.find_clusters(mm, modality="wnn", name="wnn_clusters", res=0.8)
bv.embed.umap(mm, modality="wnn")
bv.pl.embedding_plot(
    mm, "umap", "wnn_clusters", discrete=True, embd_modality="wnn", point_size=0.5
)
plt.show()

    Gene activity and label transfer¶

    Gene activity counts fragments over gene body plus 2 kb upstream into a gene by cell store of its own, the shared feature space for moving labels from an RNA reference onto ATAC cells. With paired data we know the answer: the RNA clusters of the same nuclei. Transfer them through gene activity and the ATAC LSI and count how many come back; weight_owner checks the LSI and the gene activity keep the same cells.

    In [19]:
    Copied! 
    ga = bv.atac.gene_activity(mm, fragments, gtf)
transfer = bv.annotate.transfer_labels_seurat(
    mm,
    ga,
    "leiden_clustering",
    mm.atac_cache.embeddings["lsi"],
    weight_owner=mm,
)
truth = mm.obs(cols=["leiden_clustering"], filtered=True)["leiden_clustering"]
predicted = transfer["predicted_leiden_clustering"].cast(pl.String)
agree = (predicted == truth.cast(pl.String)).mean()
print(f"transferred label equals the RNA cluster for {agree:.1%} of cells")

    Differential accessibility¶

    The marker functions take modality="atac" and test peaks instead of genes, here every WNN cluster against the rest. On ATAC the default test is a logistic regression per peak with the library size as covariate (group ~ peak + depth against group ~ depth), so a cluster with deeper cells does not light up every peak. method="wilcox" runs the Wilcoxon on the TF-IDF instead.

    Don't read these p-values as inference. Every cell counts as a replicate, so with a few hundred cells per cluster they go astronomically small with either test; use them to rank peaks. With replicates, bv.de.pseudobulk_dge(..., modality="atac") runs edgeR on summed peak counts per sample, which is the test to trust. The closest gene from annotate_peaks names the peaks.

    In [21]:
    Copied! 
    da = bv.de.find_all_markers(mm, "wnn_clusters", modality="atac", verbose=0)
annotation = mm.var(
    modality="atac", cols=["feature_id", "closest_gene", "distance_to_tss"]
)
da = da.join(annotation, on="feature_id", how="left")
da.filter(pl.col("fdr") < 0.05).group_by("grp").len().sort("grp")

    Peak to gene links¶

    A peak whose accessibility rises and falls with a nearby gene's expression across cell states is a candidate regulatory element for that gene. peak_to_gene sums both modalities over groups of cells, here fine WNN clusters, correlates every peak within 250 kb of a TSS with the gene, and tests the correlation. Fine clusters rather than the cells themselves: single cells are too sparse for a correlation to mean anything.

    In [24]:
    Copied! 
    bv.graph.find_clusters(mm, modality="wnn", name="wnn_fine", res=5.0)
links = bv.atac.peak_to_gene(mm, gtf, "wnn_fine", min_cells=10)
print(f"{links.height} links at FDR < 0.05 over {links['gene_id'].n_unique()} genes")
links.sort("r", descending=True).head(10)
